text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Vietnam does not plan to devalue the dong, Deputy Governor of the State Bank of Vietnam Le Duc Thuy told a media conference in Hanoi last Saturday.
-- French President Jacques Chirac will pay an official visit to Vietnam before the Francophone Summit in Hanoi in November 1997.
-- The State Bank of Vietnam is surveying operations of joint-ventures with state-owned commercial banks to see whether these banks have abided by regulations on capital contribution.
-- Vietnam expects to speed the disbursement of aid from World Bank and Japanese sources in 1997, Deputy Prime Minister Phan Van Khai has told a visiting member of Japan's Lower House.
-- President Le Duc Anh has granted an amnesty to Sieng Pheng, a Laotian who was sentenced to death in 1995 on charges of trafficking heroin. He will now serve a life sentence.
-- Since the beginning of this year Vietnam has received some 163 foreign investment projects from 25 countries worth over $1.64 billion.
-- The government is to hold a mid-August meeting to discuss personnel reorganisation and restructuring.
-- 15 foreign investment projects in Vietnam were licensed in July with total investment of nearly $94.2 million.
-- 400,000 hectares of the total 700,000 hectares of rice in the Mekong River Delta have not been harvested yet and are at risk from flooding.
